beginner.headline: James Bourne Says His Brother Saved His Life
beginner.brief: James Bourne plays guitar in the band Busted. In September 2025, he left a tour just before it began. He said he left because he had health problems. His younger brother Chris played in his place. Doctors told James that he had only a few years left to live. Chris later gave James one of his kidneys to save his life. James says he and Chris are both getting better. James still needs more time to get well. He calls his brother a hero.

intermediate.headline: James Bourne Says His Brother Saved His Life
intermediate.brief: Busted star James Bourne says his brother saved his life by donating a kidney. Doctors had warned him that his condition was serious and that he had only a few years left to live. In September 2025, the guitarist withdrew from a tour with Busted and McFly just one day before it began. Because of James’s health problems, his younger brother Chris replaced him. James later explained that he needed major surgery, meaning a serious medical operation, to help him live longer. Chris, who had already taken his place on tour, then donated one of his kidneys to James. James has now thanked Chris and reported that both brothers are recovering after their operations. James said he was surprised by how much better he was already beginning to feel. However, he explained that he still needed more time to recover fully. He has not shared further details about his condition. Busted had four UK number one singles before splitting up in 2005, and the full group reunited in 2015.

advanced.headline: James Bourne Says Brother's Kidney Donation Saved His Life
advanced.brief: Busted musician James Bourne has credited his brother with saving his life by donating a kidney. He described a grave prognosis, an assessment of how an illness is likely to develop, saying doctors had given him only a few years to live. Bourne, 43, pulled out of the arena tour featuring Busted and McFly on the eve of its launch in September 2025. He attributed his departure to health problems, and his younger brother Chris stepped in as his replacement. Bourne later said he needed substantial surgery to extend his life, and he has since thanked Chris as both brothers recover from their operations. Although Bourne said both brothers were recovering well after surgery, he tempered this positive account by acknowledging that he still needed time. Chris marked the outcome with a brief message on X expressing their shared achievement. Bourne has not disclosed the precise nature of his illness. He rose to prominence in the early 2000s alongside Charlie Simpson and Matt Willis in Busted, whose hits included Year 3000. The group achieved four UK number one singles before it disbanded in 2005. Bourne and Willis subsequently joined forces with McFly to form McBusted in 2013. Simpson returned to Busted in 2015, completing the original trio's reunion. Beyond Busted, Bourne has written songs for McFly and 5 Seconds of Summer and fronted Son of Dork. He also recently released music from his stage musical Murder at the Gates.
